chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, who said:

He (عليه السلام) came out to me, so I looked at his head and his feet so that I might describe his stature to our companions in Miṣr. While I was in that state, he sat and said: O ʿAlī, indeed Allah argued regarding the Imamate with the like of what He argued regarding Prophethood, and so He said:
"And We gave him wisdom while yet a child."

He said: "And when he reached his maturity," and "reaches forty years"; thus it is possible that wisdom be given while one is a child, and it is possible that it be given to him while he is a son of forty years.

key_terms.أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً: forty years of age, indicating mature adulthood
key_terms.النُّبُوَّةِ: Prophethood as a parallel divine office used here for comparison
key_terms.الْإِمَامَةِ: the divinely appointed leadership of the Imam
key_terms.الْحُكْمَ: divine wisdom or authority granted by Allah
key_terms.صَبِيًّا: in a state of childhood or young age

ai.seo_question: Can an Imam be appointed by Allah while still a child?
ai.summary: This hadith presents the argument that Imamate, like Prophethood, is established by Allah and is not restricted to old age or conventional expectations. By citing Quranic examples of divine wisdom being granted in childhood and at forty years, the Imam عليه السلام shows that Allah appoints His proof whenever He wills.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Asbat who said,

‘He (9<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) came out to me, so I looked at his<sup>asws</sup> head and his<sup>asws</sup> feet in order (to be able to) describe his<sup>asws</sup> stature to our companions in Egypt. So while I was like that until he<sup>asws</sup> sat and said: ‘O Ali! Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Argued regarding the Imamate with the like of what He<sup>azwj</sup> Argued regarding the Prophet-hood, so He<sup>azwj</sup> Said
[19:12] and We Granted him the Wisdom whilst he was a child [12:22] And when he reached his maturity [46:15] until when he attains his maturity and reaches forty years.
Thus, it is allowed that He<sup>azwj</sup> Grants the Wisdom while he<sup>as</sup> is a child, and it is allowed that He<sup>azwj</sup> Grants it while he<sup>as</sup> is forty years old’.
en.sarwar: 3. al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Asbat who has said the following “

He (abu Ja‘far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Rida (a.s.) came out to me and I looked at his head and legs so I would be able to describe him physically to our people in Egypt. I kept looking until he sat down and said, “ O Ali, Allah’s presentation of proofs in support of Imam’s Imamat (Leadership with Divine Authority) is the same as those in support of the prophet-hood of a prophet. Allah has said, “
. . We gave knowledge and wisdom to John during his childhood [19:12]. “

. . When he attained maturity, God gave him strength, wisdom and knowledge. Thus, do We reward those who do good. [12:22] “. . When he grew-up to manhood and became forty years old,. .”[46:15]. Allah may give authority to a child and He may do so when he is a fortyb years old man.”
